FUL (H.B. Fuller) — Tier 2 Review

Why it moved

FUL is down ~33% from its 52-week high ($68.63, reached after a June 26, 2026 JPMorgan upgrade to Overweight/$67) to $46.24. The decline is tied to three dateable, newsflow-driven events rather than a single air-pocket:

  • Activist pressure: Ancora Holdings made two unsolicited bids for FUL's Building Adhesive Solutions (BAS) segment — $1.1–1.2B (rejected Aug 24, 2026) and a revised $1.2–1.4B (rejected Oct 19, 2026). The board rejected both but announced a "market check" of less-core segments/product lines, which it expects to complete by year-end 2026. (PCI, Oct)
  • Leverage overhang: FUL priced an $850M senior notes offering (Oct 8, 2026) to fund its pending Advanced Medical Solutions (AMS) acquisition; $450M of the notes must be redeemed if AMS doesn't close by June 25, 2027. (SEC 8-K; Zacks)
  • Q3 FY26 earnings (Sep 23, 2026): revenue $938M (organic +4.4%), adjusted EPS $1.52 (+21% YoY, beat by ~3.7%), but the EPS guidance range was narrowed at the top end ($4.70–4.85 vs. prior $4.60–4.90) — a mixed, not clearly negative, print that the market still sold off modestly. (Business Wire; Mitrade)

1A checks

(a) Insiders — done. Tier 1's "10 open-market buys in 90 days" is 10 transactions, not 10 people. Counting distinct individuals: Malik Muhammad Shahbaz (Oct 16), R. Jeffrey Bailly (new director, Oct 7, $500K), Michael Happe (Sep 29), Celine Martin (Sep 30), Thomas Handley (Sep 28), Daniel Florness (Sep 28), Teresa Rasmussen Trangsrud (Sep 28), Charles Lauber (Sep 29), Srilata Zaheer (Sep 28 and Sep 29, same person) → 9 distinct insiders, ~$1.05M combined, all open-market cash purchases at $48.96–$52.23, clustered right around the Ancora rejection/raised-bid news (Sep 28–30 and Oct 7–16). These are directors buying stock, not RSU/option "sell to cover" — none of the buy filings show 10b5-1 plan language, and the pattern (new board appointee buying immediately, multiple directors buying the same week the activist situation escalated) reads as discretionary conviction buying, not routine. The only sells on file (Nathan Weaver, Nov 11 and Aug 11) are small, tied to option-exercise mechanics — not a red flag. Net: broad, multi-insider, discretionary buying — a genuine positive signal, similar in shape to the AMRZ precedent the framework cites.

(b) 12-month history + peers — partial. FUL's own chronology is clear and sourced (above): Perf Quarter -20.3%, Half Y -20.0%, YTD -22.2%, Year -16.6% — a multi-month grind concentrated in the last ~2 months (activism + debt raise + guidance trim), not one clean single-day event, but also not an unexplained chronic deterioration: EPS is actually growing (TTM EPS +72%, Q3 adj. EPS +21% YoY, beat estimates). That combination (price re-rating down while earnings grow) is exactly the pattern the framework flags for extra scrutiny — but here it has an identifiable, event-driven cause (leverage/activism overhang) rather than deteriorating fundamentals. I could not get a clean, sourced like-for-like peer percentage comparison against RPM/AVNT/ASH over the same window — search results were inconsistent/contradictory on exact figures (one source suggested RPM was also near 52-week lows this year, hinting at sector-wide coatings/adhesives softness, but I can't confirm this with confidence). Flagging this as unresolved rather than asserting it.

(c) Short-seller/fraud allegations — done. No short-seller report or fraud/accounting allegation against FUL surfaced in search. Nothing to disqualify on this basis.

Index rule

Finviz lists FUL's index as RUT (Russell 2000), market cap $2.49B. This is not a top-15 QQQ name nor an S&P 500 constituent — §3's index presumption does not apply, and no override catalyst is required on that basis (though one exists anyway via the activist/market-check situation).

Scores (proposals)

  • Asymmetry: 3 — statistically cheap (fwd P/E 8.98, PEG 0.86, P/B 1.15) with real event risk (leverage from debt-funded AMS deal, activist outcome uncertain).
  • Catalyst: 4 — the company's own stated "market check" of non-core segments is dated (expected complete by year-end 2026, ~5 weeks out); AMS acquisition close is also targeted by year-end, with a hard redemption trigger (Jun 25, 2027) if it slips.
  • Proof: 3 — monitorable via the market-check outcome (a dated divestiture announcement or nothing) and continued EBITDA/EPS margin trend already running ahead of plan.
  • Exit: 3 — thesis-break is definable (market check produces no deal, or AMS fails to close and leverage/redemption risk materializes, or activist situation resolves with no value unlock) but not yet written as a precise number since this is only a screen candidate, not held.

Total: 13/20 (proposal only — not yet scored as a live position).

Verdict

Watch. Insider buying is broad-based and discretionary (9 distinct insiders, not 1), no fraud/short-seller disqualifier exists, and there's a real, named, dated corporate catalyst (the market-check divestiture process and AMS deal, both targeted for year-end 2026) — this could plausibly develop into a Sleeve 1B (value gap + corporate catalyst) candidate rather than plain Sleeve 1. However, the peer-comparison leg of check (b) is incomplete, so this is not yet an entry-ready conclusion.

Gate: Check by 2026-12-31 / H.B. Fuller's Q4 FY26 earnings release (historically reported late January) whether (1) the "market check" of non-core segments produces a dated, priced divestiture announcement, and (2) the AMS acquisition closes on schedule without triggering the $450M note redemption. Before any entry decision, also re-run the peer comparison with verified, dated price series for RPM/AVNT/ASH.

NBIS (Nebius Group) — Tier 2 Review

Why it moved

NBIS closed +20.16% on 2026-11-23 (to $97.70), per Finviz day-change data. This followed a brutal multi-week slide: the stock was already down -16.11% on the single day the stored Finviz snapshot was pulled (2026-11-20, close $81.31), part of a broader "neocloud" rout (CRWV, IREN moving in the same direction on the same days per headlines). Two dateable drivers underlie the decline that the bounce is unwinding:

  • Nov 12, 2026 Q3 earnings: revenue beat ($980.8M vs ~$907M consensus, +571% YoY) but 2026 revenue guidance was trimmed to the low end of the prior range ($3.0–3.2B) on data-center capacity delays; shares fell sharply over the following sessions. [Nebius Q3 2026 release]
  • Nov 12, 2026: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately amid an espionage/affair controversy, triggering a broad AI-infrastructure selloff (NVDA, CRWV, NBIS, IREN all hit) that the Nov 20/23 Finviz data and headlines ("AI trade stocks hit hardest after Jensen Huang's exit") reflect.

I could not find a dedicated news item explaining the specific +20.2% bounce on Nov 23 itself. Given NBIS's extreme beta (4.97), 21% short interest, and RSI of 28.5 (oversold) just before the bounce, this reads as a high-beta relief/short-covering rally inside a volatile sector selloff rather than a new, NBIS-specific catalyst. No dated, named catalyst specific to Nov 23 was found.

1A checks

(a) Insiders — partial. Reviewed the listed Form 4 summary (not individual SEC filings' 10b5-1 checkboxes, so this is partial, not full verification). Distinct insiders, Oct–Nov 2026:

  • Selling (5 distinct insiders): Boynton (Director, 3 sales Oct 15–Nov 13), Boroditsky (CRO, exercised-and-sold entire 7,000-share stake twice, Oct 12 & Nov 11 — looks like routine option-exercise-and-sell), Nave (COO, 500,000 shares, Oct 5, flagged "Proposed Sale" consistent with a 10b5-1/Rule 144 plan), Korolenko (CIO, 29,090 shares Oct 1) and Shtan (CTO, 14,546 shares Oct 1) — the Oct 1 sales by three different executives at the identical price ($234.16) look coordinated/plan-based rather than panic selling.
  • Buying (1 distinct insider): Director Arne Grimme, ~12 small purchases (~$25–58K each) between Oct 15–30, cadence and size consistent with a recurring/scheduled buy plan rather than a single conviction bet — and notably he stopped buying before the Nov 12 guidance cut and the Huang-resignation crash, i.e., no insider bought the actual dip that triggered this escalation.

Net: broad-based selling (5 names) vs. one narrow, plan-like buyer. Not a bullish insider signal.

(b) 12-month history + peers — partial. Finviz stats confirm a genuine pattern, not a one-off: Perf Quarter -61.5%, Half-Year -62.1%, 52-week high -72.9% off, while Perf Year is roughly flat (-3.9%) — i.e., a huge 2025/early-2026 run that has since round-tripped via multiple separate negative events (an August 2026 "hidden AI obligations" selloff, the Nov 12 guidance cut, and the Nov 12 Huang-resignation shock). Peers CRWV and IREN fell in the same window on the same news (reported 10% and 7% drops on the Nov guidance day); I did not pull exact 12-month peer return figures side-by-side, so this is partial, not fully quantified. Qualitatively this looks like a repeated, sector-wide pattern rather than an isolated misread.

(c) Fraud/short-seller allegations — done. Michael Burry's disclosed short (initiated ~Aug 6, 2026) is a valuation/AI-buildout/GPU-depreciation thesis, not an allegation that reported financials are false. This is ordinary bear-case material under the framework, not a disqualifier. No credible fraud/accounting allegations found.

Index rule

NBIS joined the Nasdaq-100 on June 22, 2026, but at a current market cap of ~$23.8B it is far below the top-15 QQQ weight tier (which runs into the hundreds of billions per name). It is a Dutch foreign-private-issuer (files 20-F) with no evidence found of S&P 500 membership. Not a top-15 QQQ or S&P 500 name — the §3 index presumption does not apply, so no catalyst-override is required before engaging with this name on the merits.

Scores (proposals, since NBIS carries Watch status under §1 scoring)

  • Asymmetry: 3 — large upside if the AI-infra bull case re-asserts (Street target ~$237 vs. $97.70 price), but real downside from D/E 1.30, chronic negative forward EPS, and heavy ongoing capex/dilution.
  • Catalyst proximity & concreteness: 2 — no dated, NBIS-specific catalyst behind the Nov 23 move; it reads as sector-sentiment/short-covering, not a company trigger.
  • Monitorable proof: 3 — leading indicators exist (contracted backlog, data-center delivery timeline, EBITDA margin path) but next scheduled checkpoint (Q4 report) is months away.
  • Defined exit: 2 — the stated gate ("monitor capital raises and debt-to-equity swap terms") has no date and no measurable threshold.

Verdict

Funnel A — insufficient.

NBIS's own stated gate is about structural dilution risk (capital raises, debt-to-equity swap terms) — it is not dated, not quantified, and has no stated threshold. This Nov 23 +20.2% move is not actually about that risk: it's a bounce inside a broader AI-sector selloff/rebound (Huang resignation, Nov 12 guidance cut) with no evidence found that capital-raise or debt-swap terms changed around this date (Nebius has done several large convertible-note raises and at least one debt-for-equity exchange — ~15.8M shares issued against $800M of 2029/2031 notes — during 2026, but I could not confirm the timing lines up with this specific move). Per §6B, day-one price action is not the verdict, and here there isn't even a gate-specific data point to test it against. I can't respectably call this "intact," "at_risk" or "broken" against a gate this undefined — the more honest answer is that the gate itself needs to be rewritten into something measurable and dated (e.g., "next convertible-note maturity/refinancing date" or "dilution rate — shares outstanding growth — tested at Q4 report") before a future price move can actually be judged against it.

Gate to set, and when: rewrite NBIS's Watch gate before its next earnings report (historically mid-to-late February for Q4) into a measurable number — e.g., shares outstanding growth rate, net debt/EBITDA, or specific convertible-maturity dates — so a future escalation can actually be tested against it.

ROL (Rollins, Inc.) — Tier 2 Review

Why it moved

ROL is down ~43% from its 52-week high, but this is not a single event — it's the cumulative result of three separate disappointing quarterly reports in 2026:

  • Feb 11, 2026 (Q4 2025): stock fell ~10.5% on a revenue shortfall management attributed to weather.
  • Jul 22-23, 2026 (Q2 2026): stock fell ~9.3% on a miss; management acknowledged results "did not meet expectations"; this is also when Pomerantz and other plaintiffs'-firm "investigation" alerts were issued.
  • Oct 21, 2026 (Q3 2026): EPS $0.34 (slightly below consensus), organic residential growth slowed to ~2.3%; stock fell ~7%. Management tied the softness to AI/LLM-driven search changing how customers find pest-control providers ("AI-search" narrative), and this marked a second guidance cut within the year.

(Zacks; 247wallst; Tikr; Tradingpedia; Earnings Whispers — see sources)

Insider buying: on Oct 29, 2026, LOR, Inc. (the Rollins family's holding entity) bought 1,444,402 ROL shares at a weighted-average price of $34.59 (~$50M), an open-market purchase. The "R. Randall Rollins Voting Trust" Form 4 showing the identical share count, date and price is not a second independent buyer — SEC filings show the RRR Voting Trust holds a 50% voting interest in LOR, Inc. itself, and Rollins' own proxy discloses that shares held by linked entities/trustees are reported by multiple overlapping filers for the same underlying position. This looks like one family-control purchase, double-reported, not two distinct insiders.

1A checks

(a) Insiders — done, with a correction to Tier 1's framing. Effective distinct-insider count is one (the Rollins family's LOR, Inc. holding vehicle), not two — LOR, Inc. and the R. Randall Rollins Voting Trust are linked entities in the same family control structure, and the Oct 29 Form 4s describe the same 1,444,402-share, $34.59 trade. This is a genuine discretionary open-market buy by the controlling family (10% owner) following the Oct 21 selloff — a real positive signal, but much narrower breadth than "2 insiders, $100M" implies (it's ~$50M from one actor). All other Form 4s on file in the trailing 90+ days are sales by officers (CLO/GC, Chief Admin Officer, CEO, Executive Chairman), clustered on the same two dates (Jan 26 & 28, 2026) at the same prices across multiple people — consistent with routine, scheduled vesting-related sell-to-cover activity, though I could not independently confirm each is under a pre-adopted 10b5-1 plan from the data available.

(b) 12-month price/earnings history + peers — partial. Confirmed from primary/secondary sources: three consecutive 2026 quarterly reports each triggered a stock decline (Feb, Jul, Oct), with the Jul and Oct prints each carrying a guidance cut — this is a pattern, not a one-off air-pocket, matching the framework's own BSX/ZTS/IFC.TO precedent. Perf Year/YTD per Finviz: roughly -37% to -43%, against the S&P 500's roughly +15-20% gain over a similar window — material underperformance of the broad index. Peer read: Rentokil (RTO) also warned of softer North American demand and fell sharply in 2026 (Morgan Stanley cut RTO on "tougher U.S. pest-control competition," Sep 29, 2026) — so there is a genuine sector-wide softness component, not purely ROL-specific. However, I could not obtain a clean, directly comparable 12-month total-return figure for RTO (or ECL/WM) to quantify "did ROL fall more than peers" with confidence — this piece is incomplete.

(c) Short-seller/fraud — done. Spruce Point Capital published a "Strong Sell" report on ROL on Oct 4, 2023 — over three years old — alleging cash-flow/competitive-position concerns and questioning financial-statement accuracy, citing Rollins' 2022 SEC settlement ($8M, over "improper" reserve-related earnings management) and an auditor change. This is the category of allegation the framework treats as an automatic disqualifier if current and unrebutted. It is not current: it predates the entire 2026 decline (which management and analysts attribute to demand softness and AI-driven search, not disputed accounting), RBC called its issues "well known or already addressed/resolved" back in 2023, and three subsequent years of audited financials have been filed since without a restatement surfacing in my search. Separately, the 2026 Pomerantz/plaintiffs'-firm "investigation" alerts opened after the Jul 2026 miss are ordinary class-action solicitations with no named short-seller, forensic report, restatement, or regulator action behind them — per the framework's explicit carve-out, these alone do not disqualify. No current, credible, unrebutted numbers-fraud allegation found.

Index rule

ROL is listed as an S&P 500 constituent in the stored Finviz data ("Index: S&P 500, RUI"), consistent with its size and profile; I did not independently re-verify against S&P's own constituent list. Per §3, this requires a real, named, dateable catalyst before scoring. I found none: management's response to the AI-search-driven demand slowdown is a general strategic shift ("optimizing customer acquisition," testing paid ads on ChatGPT/Gemini) with no stated hard date or milestone — exactly the "we'll create value over time" language the framework distinguishes from a qualifying catalyst. The index presumption is therefore not overridden.

Scores

Not scored. Two independent reasons under the framework: (1) the §3 index presumption is not overridden (no named, dateable catalyst) — a gating condition before scoring applies; and (2) the 12-month history shows a repeated-guidance-cut pattern, which the framework's own precedent (§1A-b, BSX/ZTS/IFC.TO) treats as a reason to pass rather than discount further, independent of the index question.

Verdict

Dismiss. Two separate gates are failed: ROL is an S&P 500 member with no named, dateable forward catalyst (§3), and its 12-month record shows a chronic pattern of guidance cuts (three consecutive disappointing 2026 quarters), not a one-off dislocation (§1A-b precedent). The insider buy is real and worth noting but is narrower than it looks (one family-control entity, not two independent insiders), and isn't sufficient on its own to clear either gate. No current fraud disqualifier applies (the Spruce Point report is stale and unrelated to this decline).

Re-add condition: either (a) management or the board announces a specific, dated corporate action (e.g., a dated capital-allocation or restructuring step) that gives ROL an independent catalyst under §3, or (b) ROL posts a clean quarter with organic growth stabilizing/re-accelerating and no fresh guidance cut, ideally alongside open-market buying from distinct insiders beyond the Rollins family holding entity.
